big: Futures let you gain from a rise or a fall. They also let an investor cushion a portfolio against a fall. Which position does which?

lines: Selling a contract first. A short gains when the price falls and loses when it rises, with no upper limit to the loss. A long, buying a contract, gains on a rise. Hedging means taking an opposite position to reduce an existing risk.

intro: Made-up figures, for learning only. This is education, not a call to trade.
rows: none: price can rise without limit
Hedge: holder of shares sells index futures
note: Open interest is the number of contracts still open, for example 40 lakh at day end.

title: Long, short and hedging
stops: A long position gains when the price rises
A short position's loss is capped
Hedging reduces the risk of an existing position
caps: A short has no upper limit on loss.

q: A trader buys an index future. What is this position?
why: Selling a contract is short. It does not answer what was asked.
Buying a contract is a long position. That matches the case described.
A hedge depends on the purpose, not the side. It does not fit the facts given.
Cash settlement is how contracts end. It does not fit the facts given.

q: Which position has no upper limit on loss in theory?
why: A long's loss is limited to the price falling to zero.
A settled contract no longer exists. That does not match this case.
A lot of zero is not a position. It does not fit the facts given.
A short loses as the price rises, without a limit.

q: An investor holding many shares sells index futures. What is this for?
opts: Buying more shares of the firm
why: The short futures cushion a possible fall. That matches the case described.
It does not raise the dividend. It does not answer what was asked.
It does not buy shares. It does not answer what was asked.
Futures do not avoid all tax. The details here point elsewhere.

q: 40 lakh contracts remain outstanding at day end. What does that show?
why: Lot size is the quantity per contract.
Expiry is a date. It does not answer what was asked.
Open interest counts contracts still open.
Dividend yield is a ratio of payout to price.

pts: Long: buy a futures contract. Short: sell it.
A short's loss has no upper limit.
Hedging uses an opposite position to cut existing risk.
